rows.title: fix(core): synchronous interceptors swallow errors and proceed with request
rows.model_rationale: This changes observable behavior of the documented synchronous request interceptor feature: thrown errors in onFulfilled now stop request dispatch and route through onRejected/response interceptors, instead of dispatching anyway. The PR itself updates the changelog and doc-planning notes, confirming maintainers judged it doc-worthy, and the Interceptors docs describe this behavior.
rows.label_rationale: Changes the documented contract for synchronous request interceptor error handling (paired onRejected semantics, when the request dispatches vs. rejects). PRE_RELEASE_DOCS.md is updated in the same diff with the exact behavior to document.

rows.title: feat(types): Allow the Params property to be typed, instead of `any`
rows.model_rationale: This changes the public TypeScript surface by adding a new generic parameter P to AxiosRequestConfig and propagating it across many exported types (AxiosResponse, AxiosError, CanceledError, AxiosPromise, isCancel, isAxiosError, mergeConfig, CustomParamsSerializer, etc.). The PR itself updates the changelog and pre-release docs notes, confirming it's user-facing and documentation-relevant.
rows.label_rationale: Adds a second generic parameter to AxiosRequestConfig/AxiosPromise/isCancel and propagates it through public type declarations (index.d.ts/index.d.cts). The PR itself edits PRE_RELEASE_DOCS.md with usage examples, confirming the maintainers consider this a documented public API surface change.

rows.title: fix(core): synthesize AxiosError message from AggregateError.errors
rows.model_rationale: This fix changes the observable behavior of AxiosError.from() and toJSON() for AggregateError inputs: previously blank messages are now synthesized from sub-errors. It's a user-facing behavior change to documented error handling, and the PR itself updated the changelog and calls out docs updates for error handling.
rows.label_rationale: AxiosError.from() now synthesizes a .message from AggregateError.errors instead of leaving it blank, and toJSON() carries it. The PR updates PRE_RELEASE_CHANGELOG.md in the same diff, confirming the maintainers consider this a user-facing change worth describing.

rows.title: fix(helpers): correct data: URL base64 size estimate for maxContentLength guard
rows.model_rationale: This is a behavior fix to the documented maxContentLength guard for data: URLs: percent-embedded base64 bodies that previously bypassed the limit are now correctly rejected, and fetch now ignores URL fragments in the size estimate. The PR also adds a changelog entry (confirming user-facing relevance) and its own docs suggestion. estimateDataURLDecodedBytes is an internal helper, but the observable maxContentLength enforcement change affects real users.
rows.label_rationale: Fixes how the documented maxContentLength option is enforced for data: URLs — previously percent-encoded input could bypass the configured limit. This changes observable behavior of a documented config option.

rows.model_rationale: The fix changes the JSON Schema `pattern` emitted by `z.toJSONSchema` for `z.string().cidrv6()`, so a documented feature (cidrv6 validation / JSON schema export) now accepts real-world IPv6 CIDRs it previously rejected. This is a user-observable behavior change worth a changelog/docs note, even if the runtime intent was already documented.

rows.title: Tighten discriminated union option typing
rows.model_rationale: This is a compile-time TypeScript type constraint tightening on discriminatedUnion — options must now include the discriminator key in their input type, enforced via generics. Runtime behavior is unchanged (invalid schemas were already rejected at runtime), and the public API signature/usage for valid input is identical; the change only surfaces a type error earlier for misuse that was never valid. No documented usage, signature, or behavior for correct usage changes.
rows.label_rationale: Narrows a TypeScript generic constraint so z.discriminatedUnion() rejects, at compile time, an object option that's missing the discriminator key — a rare misuse case. No runtime behavior changes and normal documented usage is unaffected.

rows.title: fix(v4): skip __proto__ key in object catchall
rows.model_rationale: This is a security fix that changes how documented object methods (looseObject, passthrough, catchall, strict) handle a specific input shape (__proto__ key), preventing prototype pollution. Per the guidance, security fixes altering how documented APIs handle a class of input warrant a docs/changelog note, and it directly mirrors an established worked example.
rows.label_rationale: Security fix closing a prototype-pollution vector in .passthrough()/.catchall()/looseObject() (linked GitHub security advisories). This changes documented-schema parsing behavior for a security-sensitive input and warrants a docs/changelog note.

rows.title: Make z.preprocess defer optionality to inner schema
rows.model_rationale: This fixes a real, user-observable behavior change: `z.preprocess` now defers optionality to its inner schema, so `z.object({ x: z.preprocess(v => v, z.number().optional()) }).safeParse({})` succeeds where it previously failed. It also adds a new public type `ZodPreprocess`/`$ZodPreprocess` and updates the documented type hierarchy in core.mdx, confirming docs relevance.
rows.label_rationale: Introduces a new exported ZodPreprocess class and changes how z.preprocess()'s optionality is inferred from the inner schema. The PR itself edits packages/docs/content/packages/core.mdx, confirming it's a documented public API change.

rows.title: fix(v4): reject tuple holes before required defaults
rows.model_rationale: The diff changes tuple parsing behavior: previously an absent optional slot before a defaulted (required-outputput slot could succeed and truncate; now it is rejected with a validation error. This alters observable output/validation for documented `z.tuple` with `.default()`/`.exactOptional()` usage, a user-facing behavior change.
rows.label_rationale: Changes z.tuple()'s runtime parse behavior: an absent optional slot before a later required/defaulted output slot now correctly fails instead of silently truncating and materializing the default. This flips success/failure for real inputs against the documented tuple API.

rows.title: fix(v4): generalize optin/fallback to transform; restore preprocess on absent keys
rows.model_rationale: This changes observable runtime behavior of documented public APIs: preprocess on absent object keys now works again (4.3 parity restored), standalone z.transform now accepts absent object keys, and catch/transform/optional chains now clobber recovery values through pipe boundaries (e.g. catch("X").transform().optional().parse(undefined) changes from "X!" to undefined). These are real user-facing behavior changes to documented features, regardless of whether internal wiki docs are published.
rows.label_rationale: Changes how .optional() interacts with .catch()/.transform()/.preprocess() across pipe boundaries on absent input — a documented schema-composition behavior that previously produced wrong results (e.g. transform output leaking through an outer .optional()).

The fix makes the documented feature actually work for real, valid usage, which is a user-observable behavior change warranting a changelog/docs note.

rows.model_rationale: This PR adds a new public HTTP method `QUERY`, including a new `got.query`/`got.stream.query` shortcut alias, expanded `Method` and `HTTPAlias` exported types, new retry-by-default behavior, redirect body-preservation semantics, and caching exclusions. It changes multiple public surfaces and observable behaviors, and the maintainer already updated several docs in the diff.
rows.label_rationale: Adds a new supported HTTP method end to end (options type, aliases, redirect/body/cache handling). The PR itself updates five documentation files (2-options.md, 3-streams.md, 7-retry.md, cache.md, readme.md), confirming doc-relevance directly.

rows.title: Various tweaks
rows.model_rationale: This "various tweaks" PR is actually a security-relevant behavior change: sensitive headers (authorization, cookie), body, and inherited credentials are now stripped/cleared when a cross-origin change is made via prefixUrl in beforeRequest hooks, pagination, and afterResponse retries. This changes how documented features (prefixUrl, hooks, pagination, credential handling) treat cross-origin transitions for real users, warranting a changelog/docs note.
rows.label_rationale: Changes cross-origin redirect handling: which sensitive headers get stripped and when the request body is discarded/preserved after a beforeRequest hook changes the URL to a different origin. This is documented redirect/security behavior (see the cross-origin stripping notes in 2-options.md) being corrected.
